title: Slow Cooker Potato & Corn Chowder
description: Potatoes, corn, and pantry seasonings simmer into an easy creamy chowder with very little hands-on work.
substitutions: Use canned drained corn instead of frozen.
Use evaporated milk for a richer chowder.
Stir in shredded cheddar at the end if desired.

steps.text: Slow-cook the potatoes, corn, broth, and seasonings.
Mash some potatoes and finish with milk and butter.

cookSteps.text: Put 2 pounds diced potatoes, 3 cups corn, 4 cups broth, 1 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on HIGH for 4 hours, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes directly in the slow cooker. Stir in 1 cup milk and 1 tablespoon butter.
Cover and cook on HIGH for 10 minutes more, just until hot and creamy.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat gently with a splash of milk or broth.

title: Sheet-Pan Broccoli & Chickpea Pitas
description: Roasted broccoli and chickpeas tuck into warm pitas for a simple meatless dinner made from familiar ingredients.
substitutions: Use ranch dressing or hummus instead of yogurt.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 4 cups broccoli florets and 1 drained 15-ounce can chickpeas with 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon paprika, and 1/2 teaspoon salt on a sheet pan.
Roast for 22–25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the broccoli is browned at the edges and the chickpeas are hot.
Warm 4 pitas briefly. Divide the roasted broccoli and chickpeas among them and add plain yogurt if desired.

storage: Refrigerate the roasted filling up to 4 days. Store pitas separately and assemble after reheating.

title: Leftover Mashed Potato & Tuna Cakes
description: Cold mashed potatoes and canned tuna become crisp little skillet cakes for a quick use-it-up lunch or dinner.
substitutions: Use canned salmon instead of tuna.
Use crushed crackers instead of breadcrumbs.
Add chopped green onion if you have it.

steps.text: Mix and shape the potato-tuna cakes.

cookSteps.text: Mix 2 cups cold mashed potatoes, 1 drained 5-ounce can tuna, 1 egg, 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Shape into 6 small patties.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the patties for 5–6 minutes on the first side, until browned.
Flip carefully and cook 5–6 minutes more, until browned and hot through.

storage: Refrigerate cooked cakes up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet, toaster oven, or air fryer until hot.

title: Small-Batch Peanut Butter Apple Crisp
description: Two apples bake under a peanut-butter oat topping for a warm small-batch dessert with ordinary pantry ingredients.
substitutions: Use quick oats if that is what you have.
Use sunflower seed butter for a peanut-free version.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and lightly grease a small baking dish. Toss 2 sliced apples with 1 tablespoon brown sugar and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, then spread them in the dish.
Mix 1/2 cup oats, 1/4 cup flour, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 3 tablespoons peanut butter, and 1 tablespoon softened butter with a fork until crumbly. Scatter over the apples.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the apples are tender and the topping is lightly browned.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat portions briefly in the microwave or oven.
